flow_review.preflight: fresh output; initial own absent; original foreground has kernel stamp; original identity saved before child launch
flow_review.owned_binding: Popen child PID must equal FocusGuard own PID; guard supplies private bundle/path/kernel start; executable path is checked and identity saved
flow_review.cleanup: finally reacquires only matching child PID if needed; exact owned receipt passed to unchanged FocusGuard; helper verifies PID/bundle/path/kernel start, conditionally restores original foreground before exact own stop; unavailable identity refuses blind stop
flow_review.success: capture.done and live child required; helper cleanup must succeed; cleanup exception clears success; successful controlled termination may yield nonzero child exit status, which is recorded

limits: 20s ready and75s capture are phase limits, not a single global75s wall-clock cap; inspect/cleanup/wait add bounded time.

ready.json and capture.done are file-presence handoff markers. Runner does not parse ready PID/mode/window or validate captured evidence. Root collector must separately bind actual ready/output geometry and acceptance.
The original foreground restore is conditional on own being foreground; another foreground choice is preserved by FocusGuard.
Normal exceptions and Python finally cleanup are covered; this small supervised runner is not a separate external hard watchdog and cannot guarantee cleanup after forced interpreter death.

Pre-launch setup/hash failures occur before try and may leave a fresh directory without driver.json, but no app has been launched then. Helper timeout/invalid JSON may leave only partial failure evidence and no cleanup proof.
This review did not execute the driver/helper, open UI, compile, use network/git, alter source or mutate signatures. Probe implementation and runtime acceptance are outside this source review.
